hints: Focus on counting how many electrons actually sit in the outer shell of the underlined atom, not just how many bonds it makes.
Remember boron is in Group 13, so it starts with only 3 valence electrons to share in three B-F bonds.
Add up bonding plus lone pair electrons around each underlined atom and see which one ends up with fewer than 8.
walkthrough:
**What incomplete outer shell means**

Think octet rule first. For most Period 2 atoms, a full outer shell means 8 electrons. Incomplete means fewer than 8.

Rule to use:
$$\text{electrons around central atom} = \text{bonding electrons} + \text{lone pair electrons}$$

**Check boron in BF3**

Boron has 3 valence electrons and forms 3 single bonds to fluorine, with no lone pair left on B. That gives it only shared electrons.

Count:
$$3 \text{ bonds} \times 2 = 6 \text{ electrons around B} < 8$$

**Check the other underlined atoms**

Carbon in $\text{CH}_3^-$ has 3 bonds plus one lone pair from the negative charge, so $6 + 2 = 8$. Oxygen in $\text{F}_2\text{O}$ has 2 bonds plus 2 lone pairs, so $4 + 4 = 8$. Oxygen in $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ has 3 bonds plus 1 lone pair, so $6 + 2 = 8$.

All three have a complete octet:
$$\text{C in CH}_3^- = 8, \quad \text{O in F}_2\text{O} = 8, \quad \text{O in H}_3\text{O}^+ = 8$$

**Conclude**

Only boron ends up with 6 electrons instead of 8. That is the classic electron-deficient molecule, which is why $\text{BF}_3$ acts as a Lewis acid.

options.A: Correct. In BF3 the underlined B forms three B-F covalent bonds and has no lone pair. It therefore owns only 6 electrons in its outer shell, an incomplete octet. This makes BF3 electron deficient.
options.B: Not correct. The underlined C in CH3- has three C-H bonds (6 electrons) plus one lone pair (2 electrons) that carries the negative charge. Total is 8, a complete octet, like in ammonia.
options.C: Not correct. The underlined O in F2O has two O-F bonds (4 electrons) plus two lone pairs (4 electrons). Total is 8, a complete octet. Students sometimes count only bonds and forget lone pairs.
options.D: Not correct. The underlined O in H3O+ has three O-H dative and covalent bonds (6 electrons) plus one lone pair (2 electrons). Total is 8, a complete octet. The positive charge does not mean an incomplete shell, it just means one fewer electron than neutral oxygen would have in total.
